e.meaning: manly (as a short form of Andrew)
e.etymology: Today mostly a short form of Andrew, from Greek andreios, manly. An older Drew came to England with the Normans from the Germanic name Drogo.
namesakes: Drew Barrymore (actress and talk show host)
Drew Carey (comedian and host of The Price Is Right)

e.etymology: A modern spelling of Charlie, the pet form of Charles and Charlotte, from the Germanic word karl, free man. This spelling is used mostly for girls.
The Spanish and Portuguese form of Ferdinand, a Visigothic name from Germanic words for journey (or peace) and daring. Several kings of Castile and Aragon bore it.
namesakes: Fernando Tatis Jr. (San Diego Padres star)

assoc.t: Fernando, the 1976 ABBA hit song

e.etymology: The usual Italian short form of Giovanni, the Italian John, from Hebrew Yochanan, God is gracious. It is the Italian counterpart of Johnny.

e.meaning: of the Gauts, a Germanic tribe
e.etymology: From the Norman name Joscelin, a Germanic name built on Gaut, the tribe of the Geats or Goths. Brought to England as a man's name, it has been used almost only for girls since the 20th century.
Probably a feminine form built on Dan or Daniel, Hebrew names based on the word for judge. Its US rise around 2010 followed the Mexican singer and actress Danna Paola.
namesakes: Danna Paola (Mexican singer and actress, Elite)

e.etymology: An American surname anglicized from the Swiss German Brändle or Brändli, firebrand. Country singer Brantley Gilbert brought it into use as a first name around 2010.

assoc.t: Brantley Gilbert, country singer

e.etymology: The Italian, Spanish and Portuguese form of Lucian, from Latin Lucianus, a derivative of Lucius, from lux, light.

assoc.t: mob boss Lucky Luciano

e.etymology: From Old French Raimund, from a Frankish name built on Germanic words for counsel and protection. The Normans brought it to England.

assoc.t: Ray Barone of the sitcom Everybody Loves Raymond

e.meaning: from Laurentum; linked to the laurel
e.etymology: A form of Laurence, from Latin Laurentius, a man from Laurentum, a town whose name was tied to the laurel. The actress Lauren Bacall made it a woman's name in the 1940s.
namesakes: Lauren Bacall (Hollywood star of the 1940s and 1950s)
Lauren Conrad (reality TV star and designer)

assoc.t: Lauren Ralph Lauren clothing line

e.etymology: A recent name in the style of Hawaiian names such as Leilani and Kailani; lani is Hawaiian for sky or heaven and also for a chief. It is often glossed as high chief, but that reading is not well documented.

e.meaning: one who abstains; one who weans
e.etymology: From Arabic Fatima, the name of the Prophet Muhammad's daughter, from a root meaning to wean. Catholics also use it for Our Lady of Fátima, after the Portuguese town where Mary is said to have appeared in 1917.

assoc.t: Fátima, Portugal, a Catholic pilgrimage site
Fatima, daughter of the prophet Muhammad

e.meaning: dark blue; a fleet of ships
e.etymology: The English word for a country's fleet and for the dark blue of naval uniforms, from Old French navie and Latin navis, ship. It appeared as a girls' name in the US in the 2010s.

assoc.t: US Navy, the sea branch of the armed forces
Old Navy, Gap's budget clothing chain

e.etymology: The Spanish and Portuguese form of Edward, from Old English Eadweard, built on ead, wealth or fortune, and weard, guardian.
From the Irish surname O Ceallachain, descendant of Ceallachan, a pet form of the old name Ceallach, which has been explained as bright-headed or as strife.

assoc.t: Dirty Harry Callahan, Clint Eastwood's detective

e.etymology: From Hawaiian ka, the, and lani, which means sky or heaven and also a chief or royal person. It is also short for longer Hawaiian names beginning with Kalani.
A spelling of Matthias, the Greek form of Hebrew Mattityahu, gift of Yahweh, which also gave Matthew. In the Book of Acts Matthias is the apostle chosen to replace Judas.
From the English word and occupational surname for a keeper of sheep, Old English sceaphierde. Many parents choose it for the biblical image of the Good Shepherd.

assoc.t: the Good Shepherd, a biblical image of Jesus
German shepherd, the dog breed

e.etymology: First an American pet form of Chauncey, a surname of Norman French origin. It is now heard simply as the English word chance, luck or opportunity.

assoc.t: Chance cards in the board game Monopoly

e.etymology: From Greek Stephanos, crown or wreath. Saint Stephen, stoned to death in the Book of Acts, is honored as the first Christian martyr.
An English spelling of Irish Cillian, the name of several early saints, usually linked to cill, church, or to ceallach, strife.

assoc.t: George Killian's Irish Red beer

e.note: Begins with the word kill, which gives some parents pause; the Irish spelling is Cillian.

e.etymology: A Roman first name of uncertain meaning, traditionally explained as honorable. In the New Testament Titus is a companion of Paul and the recipient of one of his letters.
namesakes: Titus (companion of Paul, addressee of a New Testament letter)
Titus (Roman emperor who opened the Colosseum)

e.etymology: The Spanish and Portuguese form of Richard, from a Germanic name built on ric, ruler or power, and hard, strong or brave.
namesakes: Ricardo Montalbán (actor, Fantasy Island and Star Trek II)

assoc.t: Ricky Ricardo, Desi Arnaz's bandleader on I Love Lucy

e.etymology: From a surname that began as the Norman French nickname Rousel, little red one, for someone with red hair. It has been a steady American first name since the 1800s.

assoc.t: Russell, the Wilderness Explorer boy in Pixar's Up
Russell Athletic sportswear
Russell Stover boxed chocolates

e.etymology: A recent American spelling in the family of Aria and Ariah, written with the -iyah ending of Aaliyah. Aria is the Italian word for air and for an operatic solo.
From Old French noel, Christmas, from Latin natalis, of a birth. It has been given since the Middle Ages to children born at Christmastime.

assoc.t: noel, a word for Christmas, as in The First Noel

e.note: Usually NOH-ul for boys and noh-EL for girls; closely tied to Christmas.

e.etymology: The name of the Greek god of war, son of Zeus and Hera, whom the Romans identified with Mars. It was almost unknown as an American baby name before the 2010s.

assoc.t: Ares, war god villain in God of War and Wonder Woman

e.note: Sounds the same as Aries, the zodiac sign, and is often misspelled that way.

e.etymology: From a surname found in England and Germany that goes back to the word wild, a nickname for an untamed person or a name for someone who lived on uncultivated land. Parents today also hear the word wilder in it.

assoc.t: Gene Wilder, the original Willy Wonka
Laura Ingalls Wilder, Little House author

e.meaning: from Caesar, the Roman name and imperial title
e.etymology: The Spanish form of Caesar, the family name of Julius Caesar, which became the title of Roman emperors and the source of kaiser and czar. Its original meaning is uncertain.
namesakes: Cesar Romero (actor, the Joker in the 1960s Batman)

assoc.t: Cesar wet dog food
Cesar Chavez, farm labor leader

e.etymology: A Welsh name from Old Welsh Ris, ardor, borne by medieval rulers of south Wales such as Rhys ap Tewdwr. Reece, Reese and Rice are its English spellings.
namesakes: Rhys Ifans (Welsh actor, Notting Hill and House of the Dragon)
Rhysand, called Rhys (hero of the A Court of Thorns and Roses novels)
e.note: Said like Reese; many Americans will need the Welsh spelling explained.

assoc.t: Rhys, short for Rhysand in A Court of Thorns and Roses

e.meaning: olive tree (as a form of Olivia)
e.etymology: A modern coinage, most likely a variation on Olivia, the name Shakespeare used in Twelfth Night, usually linked to Latin oliva, olive. The A- spelling changes the first sound to match names like Alicia and Alyssa.
A Roman family name made famous by Julius Caesar. Its origin is uncertain: it may come from Greek ioulos, downy-bearded, or from the name of the god Jove.
namesakes: Julius Erving (basketball legend known as Dr. J)

assoc.t: Julius Caesar, Roman general and dictator
Orange Julius, frothy orange drink sold at Dairy Queen
